facts.big: Come in · Make yourself at home
facts.label: Receber em casa
facts.sub: Receba com Come in, please. Agradeça com Thank you for inviting me. Elogie com Your house is lovely. Peça ajuda com Can I help in the kitchen? Ouça Make yourself at home.

facts.label: Na porta
facts.sub: Quem recebe abre a porta com um sorriso e diz “Come in, please.” O convidado agradece pelo convite e entrega o presente logo no início.

facts.label: Pegar o casaco
facts.sub: É comum o anfitrião pegar o casaco do convidado e guardá-lo num armário. Em dias frios, muita gente tira os sapatos na entrada.

pages.title: Make yourself at home · 1/3
paragraphs: It is seven o’clock on a Saturday evening in Dallas. Ana stands at a blue front door with a bunch of flowers. Warm light comes from the windows. She rings the bell and waits. Her friend Ben opens the door with a big smile. He wears an apron and holds a wooden spoon.
“Hi, Ana! Come in, please.” says Ben. “Thank you for inviting me.” says Ana. “You are welcome. Let me take your coat.” says Ben.

pages.title: Make yourself at home · 3/3
paragraphs: “Thank you. The food smells great, and I am really hungry.” says Ana. “Perfect. Dinner is ready in ten minutes.” says Ben. Ben puts the flowers in a glass vase. Ana sits on the sofa and looks at the photos on the wall. The smell of chicken and rice fills the room. After ten minutes, they sit at the table. They eat, laugh and talk for hours. A warm welcome makes a happy night.
